line: Crowley’s Three of Wands: Virtue, the Sun exalted in Aries, placed at Binah.

sections.title: What Crowley names
sections.line: The chapter name for the card. The second quotation gives the element of its suit.

quotes.quote: The Three of Wands is accordingly the Lord of Virtue.
“Wands”, attributed to Fire; “Cups”, to Water; “Swords”, to Air;

sections.title: Its place on the Tree and in the zodiac
sections.line: The card refers to Binah in the suit of Fire, and to the Sun in Aries, the sign of his exaltation.

quotes.quote: This card refers to Binah in the suit of Fire, and so represents the establishment of primeval Energy.
It refers to the Sun in Aries, the Sign in which he is exalted.

sections.title: What it figures
sections.line: The Threes as a group express Understanding, and the card’s image is a lotus wand at the beginning of spring.

quotes.quote: These cards are referred to Binah; in each of them is expressed the symbolism of Understanding.
For this reason one sees the wand taking the form of the Lotus in blossom.
